falsifications.what: the seal gate (G161) required only that a SELECTED design's authority event exist; runtime::seal::gate_container never validated it against the principal registry
falsifications.demonstrated_by: core seal::gate::tests::a_design_without_selection_authority_does_not_seal: a provider's event, an undeclared principal's, an unsigned one, a signed-then-edited one and one under an undeclared key -- each ELIGIBLE with the authority check removed (mutant M1), each NOT_ELIGIBLE with DESIGN_AUTHORITY_REFUSED now
falsifications.impact: none recorded: no design has ever been SELECTED (the registry ships empty), so no seal rests on it
falsifications.fixed_by: design::authority_violations, asked by design::validate and by the gate (GateInputs.registry)

falsifications.what: a declared principal was a name, not an authentication: any writer of a design file could put a declared principal's name on its event
falsifications.fixed_by: registry keys, event signatures over signing_message, native strict Ed25519 verification

oracles.sha512: FIPS 180-4 examples (empty, abc, the 896-bit message) and a 1,280-byte input; expected digests from Python hashlib
oracles.ed25519_vectors: RFC 8032 section 7.1 TESTs 1-3; OpenSSL 3.0.13 reproduced TESTs 2 and 3 from their secret keys (pkeyutl -sign -rawin), ed25519-compact 2.6.0 reproduced TEST 1
oracles.ed25519_constants: d, sqrt(-1) and (2^512 - 1) mod L from Python big integers
oracles.differential: 24 keys and messages signed by ed25519-compact 2.6.0 (test-only dev-dependency, default features off, no dependencies): Atlas verifies every valid signature and agrees with it on each tampered one
oracles.interop: an event prepared by `atlas-systemizer design event` and signed by OpenSSL (seed 0x42 repeated) authenticates in Atlas and fails once its generation changes (core design::tests::an_event_signed_by_an_independent_tool_authenticates)

refusals_tested: SIGNING_KEY_UNDECLARED (a stranger's key; the key declared for another principal; another algorithm)
SIGNATURE_INVALID (another key's signature under the declared key; signed then edited; a flipped bit)
the identity as key or R
a universal forgery A = R = identity, S = 0
a small-order key with an honest-looking R
a small-order R under an honest key
a y with no curve point

list: M6 small-order refusal removed (A and R)
mutants.note: M6b and M6c survived the first test set (the combined forgery tripped the other check); one forgery per point was added and both are killed

boundary.signing: absent from Atlas: a principal signs outside Atlas with its own tool; Atlas never creates, declares, holds or asks for a key
boundary.registry: ships empty; nothing is SELECTED until the owner declares a principal and a key and signs
open: key rotation, revocation and signing-time bounds

oracle_choice: ed25519-dalek 2.2.0 was tried first and refused by the repository's own Cargo oracle test (adapter dependency::cargo_oracle): curve25519-dalek locks fiat-crypto behind a custom cfg no host build downloads, so `cargo metadata --offline` failed; ed25519-compact has no dependencies
